templates.name: Multidisciplinary Research Council
templates.description: A balanced team meeting for turning an early research question into an evidence-aware decision and work plan.
templates.agenda_template: Evaluate the research question: {{research_question}}. Determine what is known, what remains uncertain, the best next investigation, and the human decision the work should support.
questions: What is the most defensible current answer to the research question?
Which claims are supported by direct evidence and which are inference?
What are the leading alternative explanations?
What study or analysis would most efficiently reduce decision-critical uncertainty?
What ethical, feasibility, and reproducibility constraints apply?
What should happen next, by whom, and with what acceptance criteria?
rules: Cite stable evidence IDs for material factual claims.
Preserve meaningful disagreement.
Separate exploratory and confirmatory work.
Do not present model consensus as external validation.

templates.name: Expert–Critic Method Review
templates.description: An iterative expert and critic loop for repairing a protocol, analysis plan, or computational method.
templates.agenda_template: Review and improve the following method or protocol: {{method_text}}. Produce a corrected version and a change log.
questions: What are the most consequential methodological flaws or omissions?
Which assumptions require validation?
What controls, measurements, error handling, or reporting are missing?
What is the revised method?
What remains unresolved and requires a human specialist?
rules: The critic must reference the exact passage or step being challenged.
The expert must explain whether each critique was accepted, modified, or rejected.
Do not invent successful validation or execution.

templates.name: Systematic Evidence Map
templates.description: Develops a documented search strategy and evidence map before drawing conclusions.
templates.agenda_template: Map the evidence relevant to {{research_question}}, including terminology, inclusion criteria, study types, findings, contradictions, and gaps.
questions: What concepts, synonyms, and search terms define the topic?
What inclusion and exclusion criteria are appropriate?
What evidence clusters, consensus areas, and contradictions exist?
Where is evidence absent, indirect, or low quality?
What can and cannot currently be concluded?
rules: Do not claim the search is systematic unless documented criteria and coverage support that label.
Record source identifiers, retrieval date, and locators.
Include negative and contradictory evidence.

templates.name: Experiment Design Review
templates.description: Creates and stress-tests a controlled experimental plan with clear endpoints and decision criteria.
templates.agenda_template: Design a feasible experiment to test {{hypothesis}} under the stated constraints: {{constraints}}.
questions: What is the estimand or primary endpoint?
What treatment, comparison, controls, randomization, and blinding are required?
What sample-size assumptions and analysis plan are appropriate?
What pre-specified stop, success, and failure criteria apply?
What resources, approvals, data, and provenance are required?
What pilot should precede the confirmatory experiment?
rules: Pre-specify primary and secondary outcomes.
Identify confounders and alternative explanations.
Do not imply ethical or safety approval.
Include a reproducibility checklist.

templates.name: Computational Pipeline Council
templates.description: Designs a modular computational workflow with data contracts, baselines, validation, and reproducible execution.
templates.agenda_template: Design a computational pipeline for {{objective}} using {{available_data_and_compute}}.
questions: What are the input/output data contracts and authoritative sources?
What baseline methods must be included?
What splits, metrics, seeds, and ablations are required?
How will leakage, drift, bias, and failure be detected?
What components require sandboxed execution and human review?
What provenance is needed to reproduce every artifact?
rules: No untrusted code execution in the meeting runtime.
Specify resource estimates and fallback methods.
Do not treat simulated or predicted performance as measured performance.

templates.name: Ensemble Idea Generation + Merge
templates.description: Runs several independent high-variation councils, then uses a conservative merger to compare and synthesize them.
templates.agenda_template: Generate diverse, feasible approaches to {{research_problem}}, then compare them and select or combine the strongest elements.
questions: What distinct approaches are available?
What evidence and assumptions support each?
What are the feasibility, information gain, cost, and risk tradeoffs?
Which elements survive critical comparison?
What is the merged recommendation and why?
rules: Ensemble member runs must not see each other's outputs.
The merger must preserve minority alternatives when uncertainty remains.
Do not select an approach merely because it appears most often.

templates.name: Reproducibility Readiness Audit
templates.description: Audits an existing study or run for the information and artifacts needed to reproduce it.
templates.agenda_template: Audit {{study_or_run}} for repeatability, computational reproducibility, protocol completeness, and external replication readiness.
questions: Can every input and transformation be identified?
Are code, data, environments, parameters, prompts, tools, and manual interventions versioned?
Which steps are ambiguous or dependent on tacit knowledge?
Which artifacts can be shared and under what restrictions?
What must be repaired before an independent replication attempt?
rules: Mark each item as present, partial, missing, or not applicable.
Do not infer that an artifact exists from a narrative claim.
Prioritize defects by effect on reproducibility.

templates.name: Grant Concept Red Team
templates.description: Simulates a rigorous review panel and produces a targeted revision plan.
templates.agenda_template: Review the grant concept {{concept_title}} for significance, innovation, approach, feasibility, team, risk, and reviewer clarity.
questions: What is the strongest and weakest part of the concept?
Is the central hypothesis or objective testable?
Are significance and innovation supported rather than asserted?
What methodological or feasibility concerns would lower the score?
What revisions would most improve reviewer confidence?
rules: Use an explicit scoring rubric.
Do not manufacture preliminary results.
Distinguish narrative weakness from scientific weakness.

templates.name: Manuscript Claim Audit
templates.description: Maps manuscript claims to evidence and identifies overstatement, missing context, and reporting gaps.
templates.agenda_template: Audit the manuscript or draft {{document_name}} for evidence alignment, reporting completeness, reproducibility, and claim calibration.
questions: Which claims are directly supported, indirectly supported, unsupported, or contradicted?
Are methods and results reported with enough detail?
Are uncertainty, negative results, and limitations represented?
What language should be narrowed or clarified?
What tables, figures, citations, or supplementary artifacts are missing?
rules: Quote or locate the exact claim under review.
Never add data or outcomes.
Preserve author meaning while correcting overstatement.

templates.name: Data Management + Governance Plan
templates.description: Creates an operational data plan covering collection, metadata, access, security, retention, and sharing.
templates.agenda_template: Create a research data management and governance plan for {{project_name}} covering {{data_types}}.
questions: What data will be collected, generated, derived, or received?
What classifications, consent, agreements, and access restrictions apply?
What metadata, identifiers, formats, and quality controls are required?
Where will data be stored, backed up, archived, shared, and deleted?
How will lineage and reproducibility be maintained?
rules: Apply least privilege and data minimization.
Name an owner and review cadence for every control.
Do not route restricted data to unapproved model providers.
